blocks.text: After showing that the alleles of one character segregate, Mendel studied whether the genes of different characters also segregate independently. He examined two characters together: seed shape, with round (R) dominant and wrinkled (r) recessive, and seed colour, with yellow (Y) dominant and green (y) recessive.

items: Pure-breeding plants with both dominant traits: round and yellow seeds (RRYY).
Pure-breeding plants with both recessive traits: wrinkled and green seeds (rryy).

blocks.text: He crossed these pure-breeding plants (RRYY x rryy). All F1 seeds showed both dominant traits, round and yellow, and were heterozygous with genotype RrYy. Such F1 plants are called dihybrids, because they are heterozygous for both genes.
